claims.claim: File a written response with the court.
claims.quote: file with the court a written pleading in response to the complaint
claims.note: The statute specifies a written pleading.

claims.claim: File specifically with the court clerk.
claims.note: The filing direction names the court, not the clerk.

claims.quote: within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.
claims.note: The draft does not state a specific number of days.

claims.claim: A general denial is allowed if the complaint is unverified.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.note: This supports the type of denial, not eligibility to use a particular form.

claims.claim: PLD-050 is the short general-denial form.
claims.note: The form is named but its text was not provided.

claims.claim: PLD-050 may be used in any unverified limited civil case.
claims.note: The citation description mentions assigned claims over $1,000, but it is not the form text and does not establish whether a restriction applies to unverified complaints.

claims.claim: The limited-civil amount ceiling is $35,000, inclusive.
claims.quote: (a) The amount in controversy does not exceed thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000).
claims.note: The ceiling applies to the statutory amount in controversy, excluding attorneys’ fees, interest, and costs.

claims.claim: A claim of $35,000 or less is by definition a limited civil case.
claims.quote: an action or special proceeding shall be treated as a limited civil case only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:
claims.note: Amount is necessary but not sufficient. Subdivisions (b) and (c) also restrict the relief sought.

claims.claim: A person who cannot afford the filing fee can request a fee waiver.
claims.note: No fee-waiver request or eligibility instructions were supplied.

claims.claim: Use form FW-001 to request the waiver.
claims.note: The form text was not supplied.

flags.text: “Any” asserts universal PLD-050 eligibility. Section 431.30(d) supports a general denial in an unverified complaint but does not identify the form.

The stated scope includes verified complaints. The draft does not address them; §431.30(d) expressly requires a positive or information-and-belief denial for a verified claim assigned to a third party for collection.
The definition of a limited civil case treats the dollar ceiling as the sole test.
Neither named Judicial Council form was supplied to check the form-specific instructions.
Reliance on an unverified form-selection instruction could lead to a defective response and risk default. The supplied sources do not establish that using a particular form itself triggers default.

result.summary: The statutes support timely filing of a written pleading and a general denial for an unverified complaint. They do not establish PLD-050 eligibility or the FW-001 instruction. The draft also gives an incomplete definition of a limited civil case.
